product: ElevenLabs — text to speech, streaming (stream-input WebSocket)

source_audio.description: Locally generated signal-generator tone — NOT provider output, and no provider was called. 1404 samples of a symmetric triangle wave, period 50 samples, peak amplitude 9000, written as 16-bit signed little-endian mono at 16000 Hz (the pcm_16000 output_format ElevenLabsOptions requests by default). Generated with integer arithmetic only, deliberately: Math.Sin is not guaranteed bit-identical across platforms and this file is asserted byte-for-byte. The generator is committed as SyntheticPcm.Triangle in this suite and RecordedFixtures_ShouldMatchTheirDocumentedGeneratorParameters_WhenRegeneratedLocally regenerates the file from these three numbers on every run, so the bytes are reproducible rather than magic. 2808 bytes is 1.07% of the 256 KiB cap and is deliberately NOT a multiple of the fake's 320-byte frame size (8 full frames + a 248-byte partial), so a partial final frame reaches the consumer.

applied: voice-id path segment in the endpoint template
redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted from the file because nothing was captured: these bytes were computed locally from three published parameters and carry no vendor speech, no voice and no spoken content of any kind. The endpoint template above is placeholdered because the path segment names the voice.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — ElevenLabs is not-cleared for capturing Output, so this fixture takes the documentation-derived route, which contains no Output at all

source_schema.method: The page above was read for the server-to-client message set. It is not a transcription of any documented payload: it is a locally computed waveform in the output_format the request asks for. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied into this repository.

notes: WHY THERE IS NO REAL CAPTURE: ElevenLabs is not-cleared (protocol section 7). ToS 4(c)(ii) grants Output rights but 4(a) subordinates them to the Prohibited Use Policy, whose 9(n) bars making Output available on terms more permissive than ElevenLabs' own — MIT categorically is — and whose 9(l) bars Output used as part of a dataset for 'testing' AI, a word that appears in the prohibition verbatim. Protocol section 7 also describes an audio-payload-swap variant for this vendor: keep the REAL captured frame envelope and alignment structure and replace only the audio with locally synthesized bytes of identical length. THAT VARIANT REMAINS THE UPGRADE PATH AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE HERE, for the plain reason that it still requires a capture and no ElevenLabs capture credential exists in this environment. What is committed instead is the documented alignment STRUCTURE (see the sibling audio-output-frame.json) plus these locally generated bytes — strictly less than the swap variant, and said so rather than implied.
